newsitem.title: CHINA: China paves way for Gore with anti-U.S. blasts.
newsitem.headline: China paves way for Gore with anti-U.S. blasts.

text.p: China on Thursday blasted the United States over its stance on Hong Kong and a political funding scandal even as it started rolling out the diplomatic welcome mat for a visit by U.S. Vice President Al Gore.

The People's Daily, mouthpiece of the ruling Communist Party, accused the U.S. Congress of arrogant meddling in Hong Kong, saying some legislators were using concerns about the territory's post-colonial future to try to contain China.
The official Xinhua news agency slammed Washington over allegations that Beijing tried to illegally channel money to the Democratic Party.

The tirades were in sharp counterpoint to welcoming words from a Foreign Ministry spokesman for Gore, scheduled to arrive in Beijing next week for a visit that China is hailing as a significant step in Sino-U.S. relations.

A bill approved by the U.S. House of Representatives, calling on Beijing to honour its promises on Hong Kong after the British colony returns to Chinese rule on July 1, was pointless, unjustified and wrong, the People's Daily said.
"This once again reveals the ugly mentality of some members of the U.S. Congress who want to lord it over the world," the newspaper said.
Some congressmen were trying to use the Hong Kong issue to aid a policy of containment against China, it said.
"No sovereign government could tolerate the practice of the supercilious U.S. Congress in grossly interfering in its internal affairs," it said.
Separately, Xinhua said recent U.S. media reports accusing Beijing of attempting to make illegal campaign donations to U.S. Democratic politicians were lies spread by anti-China forces.

"Acting like someone who chases the wind and clutches at shadows, some American media took the chance to create sensational news without any fact in a vilification campaign against China," Xinhua said.
"Some members of the U.S. Congress have also made use of the matter in an attempt to cook up charges against China," the agency said.

The Washington Post reported earlier this month that the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation warned six members of Congress last year that they had been targeted by China to receive illegal campaign donations from foreign firms.

China had never interfered in the internal affairs of other nations and had neither the financial power nor the interest to spend huge sums of money on such matters, Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a regular news briefing.
The twin media jabs were the latest propaganda attacks to ruffle a Sino-U.S. rapprochement that both sides say should be bolstered by Gore's visit to Beijing next week.
"We hope Vice-President Gore's visit to China will be able to win complete success," Cui said.

Gore's meetings in the Chinese capital are intended to pave the way for an exchange of presidential visits but the new disputes over Hong Kong and political financing are potential obstacles to improving ties.
"We think the development of Sino-U.S. ties should ... rely on increasing trust, reducing troubles, developing cooperation and avoiding conflict," Cui said.
